newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish money market dry, zloty weakens vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Polish money market dry, zloty weakens vs basket.

text.p: The Polish money market remained dry on the last day of October's reseve with dealers expecting overnight rates to trade around the central bank's lombard rate of 25 percent on position squaring.
They said that despite the start of a new reserve period on Thursday banks were likely to keep searching for funds ahead of the long weekend starting on All Saints Day on Friday.
They said the demand for cash was likely to keep T/N rates above the NBP's fortnight drainage rate of 19.14 percent.
"Traders are likely to bid high for four-day T/N to avoid gaps on reserve positions," said Rafal Litwinczuk of ING Bank.
At 0900 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 24.5/25.0 percent against the opening at 24.8/25.1 percent, tomorrow/next were at 19.5/20.2 percent from opening's 19.5/20.5 percent.
Dealers said banks overinvested in the reverse repo last Friday which drained 912 million zlotys off sytem on Monday.
"Banks placed to much money with NBP on Friday," said Marek Zelinski from Bank Slaski SA.
Some overnight deals done over 25 percent signalled banks were reluctant to take lombard financing from the central bank or did not have enough T-bills as collateral for the NBP's lombard cash.
The Polish zloty was weakening in thin early trade mostly tracking the stronger dollar in European trade.
At 0915 GMT the zloty was quoted at 1.86/1.82 percent from the trading band centre, down from opening's 1.98/1.90 percent.
It was at 2.8143/50 per dollar, down from 2.8095/15 on opening and at 1.8609/18 to the mark, down from 1.8590/09.

Broad money rose by 2.89 billion zlotys, or 2.3 percent, in October 1-20 to 126.1 billion after a 1.2 pct rise in the whole of September, preliminary central bank figures showed. Polish net foreign currency reserves grew by $99 million in October 1-10 to $21.67 billion. -- Krzysztof Wojcik +48 22 653 9700
